raw_response:
I am thinking about this year like I always do — same as last year, maybe a little adjustment.

My 5 mu is not big. I am 78 now, my back is not what it was, but wheat and maize I have done forty years. The boy works in town, sends money, but the land is still mine to manage. My wife helps at busy times, and I pay the machine man from the village for plowing and harvest.

**Wheat** — I sow in early October after the maize comes off. I buy the same hybrid seed the shop sells, Jimai type, everyone in my row plants it. I use about 15 kg per mu of seed because my land is a bit tired and I want thick stand.

For fertilizer, at sowing I spread one bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15), that is 50 jin, about 25 kg per mu. Then at greening in spring I topdress urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. Total nitrogen comes to maybe 13-14 kg per mu. I do not want to spend more — urea is not cheap now. But I would rather put a little extra than see yellow wheat.

Irrigation from the well — winter water before freezing, then spring at jointing, then once at grain filling. Three times usually. If rain is good maybe two, but I do not trust the sky.

Pesticide — spray once for aphids in spring, once mixed herbicide. Two times.

Plowing — I hire the rotary machine, same as everyone. 40 yuan per mu.

Yield I hope for 500 kg per mu. Last year I got 480.

**Maize** — sow right after wheat harvest in June, no-till direct seeding with the machine, everyone does this now, saves time because the season is tight. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu type, whatever the shop has fresh.

Compound fertilizer at sowing, 25 kg per mu. Then urea at big trumpet stage, 20 kg per mu. Nitrogen about 14 kg.

Irrigation — if June is dry I water once after sowing. Maybe one more at tasseling. Two times usually.

Pesticide — one spray for corn borer, one herbicide after sowing. Two times.

Yield — I aim for 550 kg per mu. Maize usually does better than wheat on my land.
